```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(TConstrain)
```

## The observation model

Let $x_i\in\mathbb R^d$ be the observed centroid of cluster $i$. For a tree $T$,
fix one centroid $x_r$ and orient its edges away from it only to define the
conditional density. Independently on each edge,
$x_j\mid x_i,T,\sigma\sim N_d(x_i,\sigma^2 I)$.

$$\log L_T=-\frac{(K-1)d}{2}\log(2\pi\sigma^2)
-\sum_{(i,j)\in T}\frac{\lVert x_i-x_j\rVert^2}{2\sigma^2}.$$

The map from the non-root coordinates to tree increments has determinant
magnitude one. Thus the product of Gaussian increments is a normalized density
on those coordinates, rather than a collection of independent pairwise
observations on the complete graph. Symmetry makes the numerical score invariant
to reorienting a fixed tree. This is a centroid coordinate model, not a raw
scRNA-seq count model. Dimensions and increments are assumed isotropic and
independent; centroid sampling error and hyperparameter uncertainty are not fitted.

## A normalized prior and posterior

For soft rules define $b_{ij}\in\{-1,0,1\}$, representing cannot-link, neutral
and must-link. With $s\geq1$, $\alpha\geq0$, and $\tau>0$,

$$a_{ij}=b_{ij}\log s-\alpha\lvert t_i-t_j\rvert/\tau.$$

The time term is zero if either time is unknown. It is also zero by default
because `time_strength = 0`. These coefficients are specified externally; rules
selected by inspecting the same coordinates should not be treated as independent
experimental evidence.

Let $\mathcal T_H$ contain all labeled spanning trees satisfying hard rules.
Required edges must be acyclic, and allowed edges must connect all clusters.

$$Z_0=\sum_{T\in\mathcal T_H}\exp\left(\sum_{e\in T}a_e\right),\qquad
p(T\mid H)=\frac{\exp(\sum_{e\in T}a_e)}{Z_0}.$$

With $\ell_e$ the complete edge Gaussian log density,

$$Z_1=\sum_{T\in\mathcal T_H}\exp\left(\sum_{e\in T}(a_e+\ell_e)\right),$$
$$p(T\mid X,H,\sigma)=\frac{\exp(\sum_{e\in T}(a_e+\ell_e))}{Z_1},\qquad
\log p(X_{-r}\mid x_r,H,\sigma)=\log Z_1-\log Z_0.$$

Normalizing the prior matters for evidence and comparison of prior strengths,
even though its normalizer cancels when ranking trees for one fixed prior.
The evidence is a coordinate density, not a probability of the scientific
hypothesis. Compare values only with an unchanged observation space and units.

## Exact calculation and audit

Contract the required forest, remove forbidden edges and optional edges internal
to each contracted component, and keep parallel edges between components.
For either prior or posterior edge conductances, a reduced weighted Laplacian
has determinant equal to the sum of tree weight products. Required-edge weight
products multiply this determinant. For an optional edge, its marginal equals
its conductance times effective resistance; required and excluded edges have
probabilities one and zero. This is the matrix-tree calculation for factored
tree distributions [Meila and Jaakkola, UAI 2000](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.3875).

The implementation shifts log weights, uses Cholesky factorization and checks
conditioning, marginal bounds and the expected edge count. Severe underflow or
ill-conditioning raises an error. No sampling or enumeration is needed for
inference. Complexity is O(K^3) time for the dense factorization and O(K^2) memory.

```{r}
x <- rbind(A = c(0, 0), B = c(1, 0), C = c(0, 1))
fit <- fit_tree_posterior(x, likelihood_scale = 1)
fit$edges[, c("from", "to", "prior_probability", "posterior_probability")]
sum(fit$edges$posterior_probability) # K - 1
score_tree(fit, fit$map)
```

Edge marginals do not multiply to a tree probability: the spanning-tree
restriction couples edges. Use `score_tree()` to score an entire candidate.
Different optimal trees can have equal posterior mass; the MAP routine reports
one of them, while the normalized posterior includes every supported tree.

## Parameter choice and biological interpretation

`sigma = likelihood_scale` is in embedding units and defaults to 1. It is not
estimated. When coordinates are multiplied by $c$, multiply sigma by $|c|$ to
preserve topology probabilities. Reassess sigma after changing dimensions or
representation. Fix a grid using external evidence, and evaluate predictions on
withheld donors or biological measurements. Report parameter sensitivity and
bootstrap stability separately from conditional posterior probabilities.

`prior_strength` changes pairwise preferences; `time_strength` changes time-gap
preferences. Neither is a marginal probability. Hard rules dominate any soft
preference on the same pair. Avoid using a rule both to construct a model and to
claim predictive validation of it. A hard constraint fixing the full tree makes
the posterior certain by construction.

For B-cell work, distinguish transcriptional states from clonal ancestry and
from sampling time. The tree describes possible coarse branching topology,
not repeated GC zone cycling or multi-parent convergence. No cell pseudotime or
automatic Slingshot integration is implemented. The MAP optimization costs may
be negative and must not be accumulated as time or length for cell ordering.
